t: This was the site of Holy Trinity Gough Square, a Victorian church in the City of London. The building is gone now, but it was designed by John Shaw Jr., an English architect who lived from 1803 to 1870. His work was praised as being in the manner of Wren. He favoured classical Jacobean designs, and he created some of London's first semi-detached homes near Chalk Farm. He retired in the early 1860s and is buried at Kensal Green Cemetery.
